key_insight: Freestream turbulence strongly reshapes moderate adverse-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layers over an airfoil, reducing wake effects and moving skin friction toward zero-pressure-gradient-like behavior.
engineering_relevance: In realistic aerodynamic environments, freestream turbulence can materially change boundary-layer growth, drag-related skin-friction trends, and turbulence scaling, so it must be included in airfoil and wing design assessments.
method: Wind-tunnel experiments on a NACA 0015 airfoil
Angle of attack set to 2° and 4° to vary the adverse pressure gradient
Hotwire measurements taken over x/c = 0.400–0.625 with FST levels from 0.15% to 6%
evidence_signal: Across constant chord Reynolds number (~250,000), increasing FST systematically changed mean velocity profiles, lowered shape factor, raised skin-friction coefficient, and amplified both inner- and outer-layer velocity variance with energetic scales around λx/δ ≈ 13.
watch_item: These findings are for moderate APG conditions on a specific airfoil and Reynolds number, so extrapolation to stronger APGs, different geometries, or higher Reynolds numbers should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Effect of free-stream turbulence on a moderate adverse pressure gradient turbulent boundary layer developing over an airfoil
